about: The checks only an AI-side evaluation fills: rows SkyWright's own scan never measures (record reads through houseCARL's tools, supplied media, a live game's switch flips, and the discovery of existing patches). evalcontrol plans them as an overlay on a finished app scan, over the app plan's arms, and checks them with runcontrol's own rules for receipts, ledgers, plans and bundles; this list moved out of SkyWright's data/check-registry.json (registryVersion 5) in step 3 of the SkyWright / houseCARL boundary. Same schema as that registry, validated against this module's adapter vocabulary. appPrerequisites names checks of the app plan that must be settled on an arm (read from the bound app bundle's ledger) before a row here is measured or imported on it.

checks.title: Screenshots, video and schematics supplied with an identity that matches an evaluated arm

applicability.note: Media may be supplied for any evaluation; whether any was is not a property of the target.

evidence.limits: Admitted as evidence only when the item's configuration fingerprint equals an accepted receipt's fingerprint on that arm and it names its subject, state and provenance. Anything else is listed under unassessedMedia with the reason and is not evidence. Media illustrates a result; it never establishes one.

checks.title: References, links and record integrity errors across the winning order

applicability.note: A plugin with masters can name a record a master no longer defines; a master-less plugin defines everything it points at, so there is nothing to dangle.

evidence.limits: No CLI adapter. The capability is the MCP tool housecarl_check (errors family), which the controller cannot call: it is served by the in-process MCP server, not by a harness binary. The check therefore stays unsupported for the runner and keeps the evaluation incomplete until a human runs the tool and files a decision, which this check does not admit.

checks.unsupportedReason: housecarl_check is an MCP tool with no command-line entry point; evalrun composes processes, not MCP verbs.

checks.title: Meshes, textures and other assets the target's records name but the asset view does not provide

applicability.note: Any plugin can name an asset path; a record-free asset replacer can also remove one. Nothing in the footprint can rule this out, so it always applies.

evidence.limits: No CLI adapter. The capability is the MCP tool housecarl_asset_status. scopeprobe lists the model paths the target's records carry (count, first 50) but does not resolve them against the VFS, so an ESP-only arm's missing meshes stay a stated limit of the arm, not a measured finding.

checks.unsupportedReason: housecarl_asset_status is an MCP tool with no command-line entry point.

checks.title: Fields that actually differ between the winner and the records it overrides

applicability.note: A record can only be contested where another plugin defined it, which needs a master. A plugin with no masters adds records nobody else has yet.

evidence.limits: No CLI adapter. The capability is housecarl_records (aggregate, delta and tree forms), read under the merge rules the world-edit-compatibility skill states (Skyrim is not uniformly winner-takes-all, and diffing runtime-merged subrecords reports noise as findings). orderprobe measures CONTENTION — how many records a pair contests — which is not the same question and never substitutes for it.

checks.unsupportedReason: housecarl_records is an MCP tool with no command-line entry point.

checks.title: CELL attributes a later plugin restates: lighting, water height, music, flags, encounter zone

applicability.note: A CELL record in the target is the only way it can restate a cell's own attributes. Placing something in a cell carries the CELL record as a container, so this trigger fires on the container too — deliberately: the container's own fields are exactly what gets restated by accident.

evidence.limits: No CLI adapter; the same MCP record tools as records.contested-fields. waterprobe covers the CELL water tuple at a worldspace boundary only (environment.water-boundaries) — it is not a general CELL attribute reader.

checks.unsupportedReason: the CELL attribute comparison is served by the MCP record tools, which have no command-line entry point.

checks.title: Quest, dialogue and registration data: FLST membership, LCTN keywords, story-manager nodes, the dialogue graph

applicability.note: These are the record kinds that carry registration and dialogue wiring. Naming them is domain knowledge; whether the target has any is scopeprobe's measurement. A winning topic silently drops any line it does not re-list, and a form list a patch restates loses the other mod's members, so the presence of any one of these types is enough to need the check.

evidence.limits: No CLI adapter. housecarl_check findings=["dialogue"] validates the dialogue graph and housecarl_records project.form=info_order reads the merged line order; the FLST / LCTN / SMQN membership rules are read with the record tools under the skill's merge semantics. driftprobe's SPLIT class (functional.quest-alias-split) covers alias geometry, not registration data.

checks.unsupportedReason: housecarl_check and housecarl_records are MCP tools with no command-line entry point.

checks.title: Flipping the switches a mod's scripts flip, in the game, completes without a crash or a script stall

applicability.note: A runtime switch flip needs enable markers driven by a quest or script; the switch census decides which groups exist on each arm, and the evaluator writes the flip plan from the census and the bound scripts' source. Opt-in: the controller never launches the game, so this check is planned only when the caller passes --opt-in, and an evaluation without it lists it as not opted in.

evidence.limits: A run of the game under the evaluated order, in the conditions the flip plan lists (the cell loaded or not, immediate or settled). It needs a scratch game instance and is never inferable from records. A completion is 'no failure under those conditions' and never 'safe'. A finding needs at least two measured failures on the arm; one failure beside one completion is unsettled. Contention on the machine confounds timing-sensitive failures, so every launch records its idle measurement. The verdict is about the order; which record causes a failure is a separate isolation question. No claim-ledger row exists yet.

checks.title: The patch author's stated requirements and load order, read off the page

applicability.note: Advice is read from a mod page, which needs a Nexus id; scopeprobe reads it from the provider mod folder's meta.ini. No id means no page to read, and that is a measured no, not a skipped check.

evidence.limits: Run OFFLINE by default here: the stored catalogue copy is read and no network request is made, so the advice is as fresh as its recorded read date and the receipt carries that date. Cached source age is not the date the report was assembled. Per-file requirements are not exposed by the source; the stated order is advice, not a measurement.

checks.title: Patches already installed in this instance that cover the target's contested pairs

applicability.note: A patch is a plugin mastering both sides of a pair; with no masters there is no pair to patch.

evidence.limits: patchfind writes its hit list with --json (schema 1, patchfind/DiscoveryHits.cs): every plugin that masters an asked pair, with the sha256 of its file, and each download matched only by name with no hash and the reason. patch.candidate-qualification reads it. It runs per ARM because A-10(g) derives its --pair arguments from the arm itself -- the plugin pairs whose relative order flips between the baseline and that candidate -- so a baseline-only run would leave patch.candidate-qualification, which runs on every arm, blocked for want of an input on every candidate. patchfind itself reads the machine's installed plugins and takes no --order; only the pairs it is asked about change per arm. It searches the configured roots only; roots not configured are sources not searched and are listed as such. A hit is a candidate, never a verified repair.

checks.title: Installer options that fit this order and were not taken

applicability.note: Any installed mod may have a FOMOD with an unchosen compatibility option; nothing in the target's footprint predicts it.

evidence.limits: fomodprobe has no --order: it reads the instance's own installers, so it runs on the baseline profile only. With --json it writes its hit list (schema 1): one hit per plugin an unselected option delivers, with the sha256 of that archive entry, its condition plugins and its tier. Optional, because an unchosen installer option is a lead, not a defect in the evaluated order. Requires the download pool and 7z paths from the harness config; absent, it refuses.

checks.title: Downloads in the local pool that were never installed anywhere and whose masters are present

applicability.note: The pool is a property of the machine, not of the target; it is searched or it is not.

evidence.limits: poolprobe has no --order: baseline profile only. With --json it writes its hit list (schema 1): each patch-shaped plugin in a never-installed archive, one hit per archive version, with the sha256 of the extracted bytes. A downloadable hit remains UNQUALIFIED until its actual payload has been evaluated in an arm (patch.candidate-qualification).
